questions.question_text: Based on the pattern $f(x)=x^2 \implies f'(x)=2x$ and $f(x)=x^3 \implies f'(x)=3x^2$, what is the derivative of $f(x)=x^7$?

options.why: Multiplied by the power without reducing the exponent by 1.
Decreased both the coefficient and exponent incorrectly.
Reduced the power by 1 but omitted the multiplying coefficient 7.

questions.question_text: What is the inferred derivative function of $f(x)=-2x^3$?

options.why: Multiplied the coefficient by the power to get $-6$ but left the exponent at $3$ instead of subtracting 1.
Reduced the exponent correctly but dropped the negative sign, computing $2 \times 3=6$ instead of $-2 \times 3=-6$.
Dropped the negative sign of the coefficient and also left the exponent at $3$ without subtracting 1.

questions.question_text: Use the inferred power rule to find $f'(x)$ for $f(x)=3x^4$.

options.why: Multiplied the coefficient by the power to get $12$ but forgot to decrease the exponent from $4$ to $3$.
Added the coefficient and the power, $3+4=7$, instead of multiplying $3 \times 4=12$.
Added $3+4=7$ for the coefficient and also left the exponent at $4$ without subtracting 1.
Multiplied by the power without decreasing the exponent from 2 to 1.
Omitted the multiplication by the original power 2.
Changed the negative sign to positive.

questions.question_text: If a function $y=f(x)$ is a polynomial of degree $n$, what is the degree of its derivative function $y=f'(x)$?

options.why: Assumed the derivative has the same degree as the original function.
Confused differentiation with integration, increasing the power instead of decreasing it.
Incorrectly doubled the degree.

questions.solution_text:
The derivative of $x^n$ is $nx^{n-1}$, which has degree $n-1$.
$=n-1$

questions.question_text: Why do $f(x)=x^2$ and $g(x)=x^2+5$ share the exact same derivative function $2x$?

options.text: The $+5$ shifts the parabola vertically, leaving the tangent gradient unchanged at every $x$.
The constant $5$ is multiplied by $0$, which eliminates the $x$ variable entirely.
options.why: Incorrect explanation of how constants behave in functions versus derivatives.

options.text: The graphs are identical in position and have identical coordinates.
options.why: The graphs have different $y$-coordinates; only their slopes at corresponding $x$ match.

options.text: The derivative only applies to functions passing through the origin.
options.why: Differentiation applies to all differentiable functions regardless of intercepts.

questions.solution_text: A constant term shifts the curve vertically without changing its slope at any $x$.

questions.question_text: For $f(x)=x^3$, find the gradient of the curve at $x=-2$.

options.why: Squared $-2$ to get $-4$ instead of $+4$.
Evaluated the function $f(-2)=(-2)^3=-8$ instead of the derivative $f'(-2)$.
Multiplied $3$ by $2$ instead of evaluating $3(-2)^2=3(4)$.

questions.question_text: Find the gradient of the tangent to $y=3x^2$ at $x=4$.

options.why: Evaluated the $y$-value $y=3(4)^2=48$ instead of the derivative $\frac{dy}{dx}$.
Differentiated $x^2$ as $2x$ and evaluated $2(4)=8$, omitting the coefficient $3$.
Found the derivative formula $6x$ and omitted substituting $x=4$.
